# Customize Sites {#sec-site-customization}

## Goal

Use scripts in advanced site configuration, or scripts under site plugins, to hide, remove, and rewrite pages, data, and interfaces inside a site.

## 1. Advanced Site Configuration

Go to:

```text
Site Management > Site List > Configuration
```

Script-related configuration and terms include:

| Configuration | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Request headers / response headers | Allows scripts to read specified headers |
| Page script | Select `Page Script` when the script operates on page content, such as DOM, forms, buttons, redirects, and page enhancements |
| SSE script | Select `SSE script` when the script rewrites server-sent event streams |
| Standard interface interception | When neither of the above two options is selected, the script rewrites standard non-SSE interface response bodies |

## 2. Scripts and Plugins

Operation path:

1. Click **Manage Plugins** in the site list.
2. Create a plugin.
3. Fill in the name, version, remarks, and associated site.
4. Upload the plugin or enter configuration.
5. Add a script.
6. Set the matching URL, script type, selector, and content.
7. Verify with a test account.

Scripts can also be used for account types, workspaces, and inner sites.

## 3. Sensitive Page Content Controls

Suitable for:

- Hiding prices.
- Hiding customer privacy fields.
- Removing buttons and areas that employees are not allowed to operate.
- Hiding page areas for specific URLs.
- Rewriting a page area.

Selectors may become invalid after the target site changes, so regression testing is required.

## Page Script Tool

Writing and testing scripts directly on the web page is not convenient. You can download the official script editor from GitHub: https://github.com/sa2web/sa2web-script-editor.

After downloading and extracting the installation files, click `sa2web.exe` to start the script editor, as shown in @fig-sa2web-script-editor.

![Sa2web script editor](/images/sa2web-script-editor.png){#fig-sa2web-script-editor}

The following two examples demonstrate the feature.

## Example 1: Change the Official Website Header Background to Coral

1. Enter `https://www.sa2web.com` in the URL field.
2. Select `Page script`, which means the script operates on page content.
3. Enter `*` in `CSS/XPath selector`, which means the script below runs when a matching element appears on the page.
4. Enter the following JavaScript code in the script box, as shown in @fig-script-background:

```JavaScript
// Please write your code here...
// Execute the event listener function when the header element appears on the page.
api.dom.addConnectListener("header", () => {
  // Find the header element on the page.
  const header = api.dom.querySelector(document, "header");
  // Change the background color of the header element to lightcoral.
  header.style.backgroundColor = 'lightcoral';
});
```

![Sa2web background-color script](/images/script-background.png){#fig-script-background}

Click **Run Script** to test the script. The website on the left opens and the script runs, as shown in @fig-script-editor-run-script.

![Sa2web script test result](/images/script-editor-run-script.png){#fig-script-editor-run-script}

After the result meets expectations, copy the content above into the page, as shown in @fig-edit-script-on-page.

![Sa2web fill script into advanced site configuration](/images/edit-script-on-page.png){#fig-edit-script-on-page}

Click **Add**, then click **Save Config**. When users log in and access the site from the frontend, the navigation bar turns coral, as shown in @fig-official-change-background.

![Sa2web frontend access result](/images/official-change-background.png){#fig-official-change-background}

## Example 2: Show Page Views in the Middle of the Official Website

This example mainly uses `api.user` to store and display data, with persistent storage in the database. Here it is used to show a page-view counter on the official website page, as shown in @fig-script-add-page-count.

```JavaScript
api.dom.addConnectListener('body', async (con) => {
  if (window != window.top) return;
  if (window.isCounted) {
    return;
  }
  window.isCounted = true;
  // Count page views by current site only.
  await api.user.incr('counter', 1, true, false, false);
  // Get page views by current site only.
  const ret = await api.user.get('counter', true, false, false);
  document.body.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', `<div style='position: fixed;background-color:red;color:white;left:50%;top:50%;width:100px;height:100px;line-height:100px;text-align:center;font-size:50px'>
  ${ret.value}</div>`);
});
```

![Sa2web add page-view counter script](/images/script-add-page-count.png){#fig-script-add-page-count}

About one minute after clicking **Add** and **Save**, access the site from the Sa2web frontend. A red box appears in the middle of the page, showing the page-view count. Each visit or refresh increases the count by 1, as shown in @fig-script-page-count.

![Sa2web page counter effect](/images/script-page-count.png){#fig-script-page-count}

Of course, `api.user` provides more APIs than these. It can also store and retrieve data by account and by device. See @sec-script-api for the complete API.

These two examples only demonstrate some of the most basic site customization features. You can also integrate deeply with enterprise systems through other APIs, such as `api.http`, to provide a better experience.

## 4. `window.api`

Page scripts and standard interface interception scripts can use:

```ts
window.api
```

It mainly includes APIs related to `user`, `dom`, `utils`, `config`, and `header()`.

For the complete interface, see @sec-script-api.
